in_arabic.name: عمّار

in_urdu.name: عمّار
in_urdu.meaning: جو زندہ رہتا ہے اور باقی رہتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: عمّار کا مطلب ہے جو زندہ رہتا ہے اور باقی رہتا ہے، یہ نام قرآن پاک میں سورہ بقرہ میں آیا ہے، اور یہ نام فعل عمّر سے ماخوذ ہے، جو زندہ رہنے اور باقی رہنے کی دلالت کرتا ہے، اور یہ نام اسلامی روایت میں اہم ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ammaar" may be of Arabic origin and is widely used within the Islamic community across the globe. It carries an inherent sense of strength and resilience, which aligns well with the values of many Islamic cultural and historical figures. For instance, in Islamic history, there is a famous Islamic scholar named Ibn Ammar Al-Qurashi who was known for his enduring curiosity and love for knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Ammaar" holds a deeper meaning inspired by Islamic teachings. The name "Ammaar" can be derived from the Arabic word "amr," meaning command or order. In the context of the Islamic faithful, being a commanded servant of Allah, it has a spiritual significance that all devout Muslims should strive to uphold. The name might serve as a reminder of the spiritual importance of patience and perseverance as exemplified in the Quranic verse, "And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain commands, he fulfilled them. He it is who said, 'Indeed, I will make you the Imam [leader] of my people after you and increase you greatly.' [So] ask Me not about that which is to come after it." [Surah Al-Baqarah 13:24]. The verse teaches that even in the face of adversity and hardship, we should remain steadfast and faithful to Allah's commands.
